service: Potholes and road repair on county roads
how_it_depends: County roads: the county. Report to the county highway office or the SJC311 app.
notes: Accountable offices: commissioners handle county roads and bridges (office_types). Which department sits under which official is not in the guide's data.

service: Potholes and road repair on city streets
how_it_depends: City streets: the city. In South Bend, Streets & Sewers handles most streets inside city limits; the city aims for a 72-hour response outside the street-cleaning season. Who owns the road decides who fixes it.
notes: Mishawaka streets are not in the guide's data (see gaps). Accountable office: the mayor runs city departments (office_types).

service: Streets, snowplowing and leaf pickup in Mishawaka
how_it_depends: Mishawaka's Central Services Division maintains city streets and alleys and handles snowplowing and curbside leaf collection. Problems can be reported on the city's online Report a Problem form.
contact: Central Services Division, (574) 258-1660; Report a Problem form on mishawaka.in.gov
notes: Accountable office: the mayor runs city departments (office_types). Street lights are a category on the city's problem form, but no page read names the department that maintains them.

how_it_depends: Collection is listed among the city's Central Services duties; missed pickups and other trash or recycling problems are reported directly to Republic Services through the link on the city's Report a Problem page.
contact: Republic Services (link on the Mishawaka Report a Problem page); Central Services, (574) 258-1660

service: Electric, water and sewer service in Mishawaka
how_it_depends: Mishawaka Utilities, owned by the city, runs electric, water and wastewater service, with one business office for billing.
contact: Mishawaka Utilities business office, (574) 258-1630; electric outages 574-258-1649
notes: The city Board of Public Works and Safety also sits as the Utility Board (appointed_boards.csv).

service: Potholes and road repair on state routes
how_it_depends: State routes (examples named by South Bend 311: SR 23 segments, SR 933 / US 31 Lincoln Way East): the Indiana Department of Transportation, even inside a city.
contact: INDOT4U 24/7 customer service line, 1-855-INDOT4U (1-855-463-6848), or "Report a Concern" in INDOT's online Customer Service Portal
notes: indot is not a unit in units.csv. Accountable official is not sourced here. The number shown is from INDOT's own INDOT4U page (2026-11-08); the two different numbers from earlier sources were not found on INDOT pages.

how_it_depends: Inside the City of South Bend and for any property with a 5-digit address in the county: the county Building Department. Mishawaka's own building authority was not checked. Inside Mishawaka, permits and contractor licenses come from the city's own Building Department.
contact: County Building Department (sjcindiana.gov/1085); Mishawaka Building Department, (574) 258-1607
notes: Accountable official not named in the source.

how_it_depends: Zoning ordinances are listed on the county site for the county and for the towns of Lakeville, New Carlisle, North Liberty, Osceola and Roseland. Area Plan Commission and Area Board of Zoning Appeals meet monthly. Walkerton, Indian Village, South Bend and Mishawaka are not listed there. The county Area Plan Commission covers only the unincorporated county (5-digit addresses) and the towns of Lakeville, New Carlisle, North Liberty, Osceola and Roseland. Mishawaka runs its own planning through its Planning and Community Development department, Plan Commission and Board of Zoning Appeals; South Bend is also outside the Area Plan Commission's area.
contact: County Planning and Zoning (sjcindiana.gov/1883); Mishawaka Planning and Community Development, (574) 258-1625
notes: The Area Plan Commission is an appointed board (appointed_boards.csv); no single elected official is named. South Bend lists its own Plan Commission and Board of Zoning Appeals on its boards page (gap-fill B lead, not re-read 2026-11-08). The APC's 2019 annual report still listed a South Bend mayoral appointee; the 2026 member list does not.

service: Property assessment, appeals and tax bills
how_it_depends: The county Assessor values property (with an appeals board); the Auditor and Treasurer handle the tax bill and payment. Township assessors also appear on the 2026 ballot (Penn Township).
notes: Township assessor offices other than Penn Township are not in the guide's data.

how_it_depends: The County Election Board runs county and municipal elections, including candidate filings. It has two members from the major parties and the County Clerk as secretary.
contact: 574-235-9635; voter@sjcindiana.gov; County-City Building, 4th Floor, 227 W. Jefferson Blvd., South Bend 46601
notes: Accountable office: County Clerk (secretary of the board).

how_it_depends: The County Clerk's page covers courts, e-filing, marriage and divorce information and copies of marriage licenses and divorce decrees. The step of issuing a marriage license is not separately confirmed.

service: Public health (food, septic, lead, birth and death records, immunizations)
how_it_depends: The County Health Department. Its page does not say whether South Bend and Mishawaka are covered.
notes: Governed by the appointed Board of Health (9 seats in appointed_boards.csv); no single elected official is named.

how_it_depends: The St. Joseph County Parks Department, with a Parks Board and Parks Foundation. City parks departments were not checked.
Mishawaka's Parks and Recreation department runs the city's more than 25 parks, under the city Board of Parks and Recreation.
notes: The parks board's appointing authorities are in appointed_boards.csv (mishawaka-parks-board).

how_it_depends: It depends on where you are. The Humane Society of St. Joseph County holds the animal control contract for the county, Mishawaka and the towns of Osceola, Lakeville, New Carlisle and North Liberty (and Notre Dame, St. Mary's and Holy Cross), but it does not serve South Bend city limits; South Bend residents should contact the city (South Bend 311).
contact: Humane Society Department of Animal Control, (574) 255-4726; in South Bend, South Bend 311
notes: Walkerton, Roseland and Indian Village are not named in the Humane Society's contract list. South Bend's Animal Resource Center details are from the gap-fill B report (not re-read 2026-11-08).

service: Fire protection and ambulance outside the cities
how_it_depends: It depends on the township. Reports describe a St. Joseph County Fire Territory (Warren Township and unincorporated Portage Township, with its own ambulance service since 2025), a Clay Fire Territory, Penn Township, a volunteer unit in Madison Township and Liberty Township ambulance service in North Liberty. The county contracts South Bend for advanced life support ambulance outside the city, and that arrangement was uncertain after a February 2026 hearing. Centre Township is forming its own fire territory effective Jan 1, 2027 (draft resolution).
notes: News and a draft resolution, not read in full. Verify the arrangement for your address. Townships not named here are not covered by this row.

how_it_depends: Apply in the township where you live. The state housing agency says trustee duties go beyond aid to fire protection, cemeteries and parks.
contact: Union Township: 117 S Main St, Lakeville; (574) 784-3110. Centre, German, Greene, Harris, Liberty, Olive and Penn township office contacts are on each township's page in this guide. Clay, Lincoln, Madison, Portage and Warren: not found.
notes: Contact details for eight townships come from township or in.gov township pages (2026-11-08).
